items.issue: prd.enter self-recovery after a committed backlog->wip rename records source: "wip", not the original "backlog": nothing in the controller remembers the interrupted attempt bucket, so a rollback to the origin bucket is impossible. Cycle-2 review asked the recovery test to assert source: backlog; the test now asserts the shipped truth with a comment.
items.reason: needs a controller change (lifecycle.enter must record the origin bucket), which is out of scope for a test-only rework task

items.issue: Review acceptance is not enforced: a phase.handoff review->done converged claim is accepted with no recorded review evidence. Pinned by a strict xfail in tests/autopilot/test_controller_rework13_lifecycle.py (reason: review acceptance deferred to AP 00020).
items.reason: the PRD Risks section states acceptance is unavailable until AP 00020 lands the review evidence family; the strict xfail turns red the day it is implemented

items.detail: saga ops (prd.enter/stall/park/defer/complete, phase.handoff) write their replay receipt in a second transaction after the saga commits; a crash between the two means a replay gets revision_conflict/rejected_evidence instead of the cached response, and a full receipt cache (4096 entries) at that point yields recovery_required instead of the real result. files.stall/park/defer_record/complete_prd do not check the authorizing actor binding against the revision at saga-commit time (only enter/handoff do, via their own expected-revision commit), so a lease change between authorization and saga execution is not guarded for those four. lifecycle.complete calls require_recovery_idle first, so a crashed prd.complete saga cannot be resumed through the protocol today. None of these block the PRD acceptance criteria (manual_session_handoff/false_success_no_advance/drained_vs_ineligible/job_claim_exclusive/job_plan_stable/no_controller_spawn/record_exit idempotent replay all pass); flagged for a follow-up PRD.

workflow-v1.json contract JSON schema ($defs/state, $defs/response/core_result, and the runtime_validation prose) still describes the pre-AP00019 narrow state/response shapes (work: null only, empty tasks/jobs, three owner-only result shapes, frozen-workflow-reserves prose) even though schema.py and protocol.py now accept/produce the richer shapes this PRD adds. Request-shape validation ($defs/request, payload $defs) was updated and is now accurate; the state/response/runtime-prose side was out of this tasks scope. Flagged for a follow-up contract-hygiene task rather than silently left inconsistent.

No test covers a second PRD.
